newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Nov 6.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- TELECOMS MANAGERS SHARE 100 MILLION DOLLARS

In an effort to persuade top executives to stay after a 13 billion stg merger deal British Telecom and MCI are set to offer "loyalty" bonuses. MCI has set up a 100 million dollar bonus pool, along with other incentives for senior managers. BT say it is looking at ways to develop a scheme of "retention bonuses" for key executives. Chairman of BT, Sir Iain Vallance, and his opposite at MCI, Bert Roberts, say the incentives are needed to reduce the risk of top managers being poached.
-- ANGLIAN LOOKS TO RAISE 150 MILLION STG FOR CAPITAL SPENDING

Anglian Water is considering plans to raise up to 150 million stg to fund spending plans for its regulated business. The company is not considering joining the trend towards multi- utility businesses, after considering the takeover of an electricity company. Anglian is looking at making a bid for either East Midlands or Yorkshire Electricity. Finance director Chris Mellor said the company will borrow money later this year to finance its 340 million stg capital expenditure plans.
-- CABLE RIVALS RENEW ATTACK ON NEWS CORP

Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation has confirmed it has raised one billion dollars to fund its American expansion. This comes as the media empire is attacked by the British cable television industry for continued abuse of its monopoly position. TeleWest and Nynex are joining rivals in condemning the way BSkyB structures and charges cable operators to broadcast their channels. They claim BSkyB's terms and conditions undermine consumer choice, impede new entrants and may require pay-TV consumers to be charged for BSkyB services whether or not they want them. The Office of Fair Trading is considering the comments.
THE TIMES
-- AL FAYED BUYS 25 PERCENT STAKE IN ALPHA AIRPORTS FOR 52 MILLION STG

Mohamed Al Fayed, owner of Harrods and Punch magazine, has purchased 25 percent of Alpha Airports from Granada for 52.3 million stg. He may be planning to launch a full offer for the tax-free airport retailer and flight catering group next year. Alpha expected Granada to sell its stake to an airline or catering group. Alpha say that the directors had no immediate comment about Mr Fayed's arrival.
-- MARKS AND SPENCER TO TAKE ON 2,000 NEW STAFF

In a push to improve levels of service in its stores Marks and Spencer is to take on 2,000 new staff this year. Shares in the group have tumbled due to worries about increased overheads. Chairman Sir Richard Greenbury said the decision was taken because he wanted to grow the business and keep customers' confidence. He also said consumer confidence was returning so the group is working with suppliers to drive sales harder. The new jobs will be created in existing stores that are being expanded.
-- BA WINS AIR LIBERTE FIGHT AS PROFITS RISE TO RECORD

British Airways has won the right to rescue the insolvent French airline Air Liberte from Richard Branson's Virgin Express. A French court backed BA's plan to invest 55 million stg for a two-thirds stake in Air Liberte. The news came after BA had announced record year profits, with a fall in operating profits. BA hopes the French airline will help it to make money from its existing French operation, TAT European Airlines. BA also hopes to expand the airline.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SURGING STERLING HITS SHARES

The pound has been sent soaring on the foreign exchanges due to strong growth, rising oil prices and an anti-inflationary rise. Sterling is now at its best level for three years. Government securities were in demand, rising by one pound stg on the back of the City's perception that Chancellor Kenneth Clarke was prepared to take a tough line on inflation, despite the forthcoming General Election. Sterling's recent strength will feature in the Bank of England's inflation report to be published today.
-- MYSTERY FIRM IN ONE BILLION STG BET ON MARKET CRASH

Speculation has swept the stock market as it emerged that an un-named institutional investor, thought to be one of the UK's large life assurance companies, has taken a one billion stg bet on a market crash. In an options transaction on the London International Financial Futures Exchange the institution wagered that the FTSE-100 index of top companies is likely to fall by more than 15 percent between now and June 1997.
-- SIB SIT ON TWO MILLION STG COMPENSATION

Arthur Anderson, liquidator for Knight Williams, the defunct retirement advisor, have told a meeting of investors and creditors that it would be unable to settle their claims until the Securities and Investments Board decided to release two million stg of the firm's money. The money was set aside for investors under an earlier compensation scheme established by SIB. SIB is believed to be sitting on the money to protect it from the claims of other creditors, such as Knight Williams employees and directors, who take precedence over investors.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BT TIPPED TO WIN ONE BILLION STG ARMED FORCES PHONE CONTRACT

The Ministry of Defence will announce in the House of Commons that British Telecom has beaten Racal Electronics in a battle to win a one billion stg contract to replace the private telephone network, called Defence Fixed Telecommunications System, used by the armed forces. The MoD has reduced the cost of running the system from 200 million to 175 million stg and is seeking further cuts of 40 million stg. The other condition is that the web of 51 separate networks should be replaced by a single digital network by 2000.
-- BA ACCOUNTS DEBT SENT TO BOMBAY TO SAVE ON WAGES

Due to wages levels in India being one-fifth of those in Britain British Airways is to transfer part of its accounting operations to Bombay. This is part of BA's global efficiency drive aimed at producing saving of one billion stg a year by the end of the decade and will mean 5,000 job losses. Finance director Derek Stevens said that it was a lot cheaper employing people in India. Chief executive Bob Ayling said the airline was looking to outsource more activities.
-- MAM CHIEF BACKS CHEAPER UNDERWRITING

Chairman of Mercury Asset Management Hugh Stevenson is backing moves to introduce competition into the underwriting commissions charged for rights issues. This comes as Schroders launches its second cut-price financing in five days. The group auctioned 36 percent of the underwriting for a 48.6 million stg rights issue for More Group to help fund the acquisition of Wennergren Williams. The auction saved the company 109,000 stg at the expense of investing institutions such as MAM. Mr Stephenson said he welcomed anything that gave a freer system for underwriting.
